title: Bakken: VIIRS night flare power vs reported flared gas volume
one_liner: Satellite flare power tracks officially reported flared volume in the Bakken at annual/seasonally-adjusted scale, but month-to-month changes are mostly noise.

datasets.name: NASA GIBS WMTS vector tiles: VIIRS 375 m thermal anomalies (SNPP/NOAA-20/NOAA-21)
North Dakota DMR monthly gas produced/sold/flared 1990-2026

mechanism: Flared gas burns at ~1600-2000 K; VIIRS I4/M13 radiance at night gives fire radiative power roughly proportional to flared volume.
method: SNPP-only night detections 2012-02..2026-08 from keyless GIBS tiles, 0.02 deg cells lit on >=N nights, monthly statistic of nightly FRP sums; metric variant (frp_p90|min3) chosen on 2012-2018 only; log-log OLS trained 2012-2018, tested 2019+; month fixed-effects variant; rolling-origin yearly refits vs a persistence baseline.

results.note: attenuated well below 1: FRP is a noisy regressor

controls: Train/test split in time; metric variant chosen on train only; persistence baseline; deseasonalising and differencing reported alongside levels.
known_or_novel: known (VIIRS Nightfire literature calibrates flare radiant heat to volume); the keyless replication and the honest monthly-change null are ours
caveats: State-level label vs basin bbox; Texas V&F is operator-reported and lagged; FIRMS FRP is not Nightfire radiant heat (no temperature fit); satellite series carries a 4-7x seasonal artifact absent from the label.

title: US shale: flare power as a gauge of crude production
one_liner: In US shale basins flare power says almost nothing about monthly crude output; flaring is driven by gas-takeaway constraints, not barrels.

datasets.name: NASA GIBS WMTS vector tiles: VIIRS 375 m thermal anomalies (SNPP/NOAA-20/NOAA-21)
EIA crude production by state, monthly

mechanism: Hypothesis: more oil -> more associated gas -> more flaring. In practice flaring depends on pipeline/processing capacity and regulation.
method: Same monthly SNPP metrics vs EIA state crude production (ND; TX+NM).
controls: Differencing and deseasonalising; same pipeline that does track flared volume.
caveats: State production is not basin production; YoY correlations of 0.3-0.5 reflect the shared 2014-16 and 2020 cycles, not a usable gauge.

title: Does clear-sky normalisation rescue the gauge? (tested against a gold label)
one_liner: Per-cell clear-sky normalisation barely improves fit to reported flared volume, and the satellite series has a 4-7x seasonal swing that cloud does not explain; strict clear-sky filters are biased because flares themselves lower clear-sky confidence.

datasets.name: NASA GIBS WMTS vector tiles: VIIRS 375 m thermal anomalies (SNPP/NOAA-20/NOAA-21)
NASA GIBS WMS VIIRS night clear-sky confidence (SNPP 2012+, NOAA-20 2018+)
North Dakota DMR monthly gas produced/sold/flared 1990-2026

mechanism: Cloud blocks the 4 micron signal, so detections should scale with observation opportunity.
method: Nightly SNPP clear-sky-confidence grids (5,297 nights) sampled at active Bakken flare cells; monthly FRP divided by observable fraction (conf>0.05), by strict clear fraction (conf>=0.95), and clear-nights-only; compared to ND DMR flared volume. Gulf: P(detect) by confidence bin at 1,177 persistent NOAA-20 flare cells.

results.metric: Bakken r MoM dlog raw -> best normalised
Bakken r deseason+detrend raw -> conf>=0.95 normalised
seasonal amplitude of satellite series (max/min month) raw / normalised / label
results.note: observable fraction is HIGHER in winter when FRP is lowest, so cloud is not the cause
share of cell-nights 0.285, mean FRP 1.69 MW
share of cell-nights 0.158, mean FRP 10.16 MW
share of cell-nights 0.241, mean FRP 5.45 MW
share of cell-nights 0.219, mean FRP 1.97 MW
share of cell-nights 0.097, mean FRP 1.49 MW

controls: Gold label (ND DMR); same overpass for detections and mask.
known_or_novel: novel (small): the cloud mask is contaminated by the target - detection probability and FRP peak at intermediate confidence, only conf<=0.05 suppresses detection
caveats: Cloud mask over snow at night is itself unreliable; cause of the seasonal artifact not identified (candidates: background temperature, summer twilight at 48N, atmospheric transmission). Use YoY or month fixed effects instead.

title: Country-month flare power vs crude production, 16 countries 2012-2024
one_liner: Flare power tracks production only where routine associated-gas flaring is heavy and the production move is a collapse (Libya, Yemen, Iran, Iraq); in low-flaring-intensity producers (Saudi, Kuwait, UAE, Qatar, Oman) the correlation is zero.

mechanism: Routine flaring of associated gas scales with oil lifted; where gas is captured, flares are safety/process flares unrelated to output.
method: SNPP night detections in persistent flare cells (>=24 nights, >=180-day span) per country, monthly mean nightly FRP, SNPP outage days removed; vs EIA monthly crude. Quarterly non-overlapping YoY dlog panel; country-cluster bootstrap; mismatched-country placebo; split by flaring intensity (FRP per kb/d, chosen ex ante at 0.25).

title: Named natural experiments: does flaring fall when production is knocked out?
one_liner: Sustained collapses show up nearly 1:1 (Libya 2020 -89%/-89%, Yemen 2015 -90%/-90%, Iran sanctions -41%/-30%), managed OPEC+ cuts do not, and acute outages at gas-handling-heavy producers make flaring go UP (Abqaiq +122%, Kazakhstan +44%/+305%).

datasets.access: keyless bulk (API itself needs a key)

mechanism: Shut-in wells stop flaring; but when processing/export infrastructure trips while wells keep flowing, gas is diverted to flare.
method: 21 pre-specified (country, pre-window, event-window) episodes; % change in mean monthly flare FRP vs % change in EIA production.

results.metric: Libya 2014-16 civil war low: production % / flare %
Kazakhstan Aug-2022 Kashagan/Tengiz outage: production % / flare %
Nigeria 2016 Niger Delta Avengers: production % / flare %

controls: Windows fixed before looking at flare data; all episodes reported including failures.
known_or_novel: known for Libya/Yemen-type collapses; the sign flip for acute outages is documented anecdotally (Payne 2026: Iran flaring up)
caveats: Short windows are not seasonally controlled; Venezuela (-77% production, flat flaring) and Syria (-85%, flat) are outright failures of the gauge; n=21.

title: Given an X% flare drop sustained for a quarter, what production change does history imply?
one_liner: Only flare drops deeper than ~50% carry information (median production -36%, but 10th-90th percentile -88%..+16%); drops of 15-50% imply a median production change of about -1%. The pooled calibration failed out-of-sample on the 2026 war.

title: How fast does the flare gauge flag a regional shut-in, and how often does it cry wolf?
one_liner: A 7-day clear-sky-normalised alarm fired for Basra 7 days after the war began (10 days for the 14-day window) and stayed on for 84-91% of the closure; controls fired 0-5% of the time; Kuwait, Saudi and UAE never alarmed despite 25-70% production losses.

title: Reported vs observed: 72 dated physical events scored against VIIRS active fire
one_liner: VIIRS 375 m active fire sees 21% of reported strikes (28% at non-flare sites, 13% at permanent-flare sites); the detector almost never false-alarms, so the misses are real non-detections, and cloud does not explain them.

mechanism: A strike that ignites hydrocarbons produces a multi-MW thermal anomaly visible at the next overpass if it is still burning, unobscured and outside an existing flare footprint.
method: Event list (66 war events + 6 from June 2025) compiled from Wikipedia/HRW by sub-agents with no access to hotspot data; coordinates from OSM / pre-June-2025 flare clusters / approximate. Detector: novel 0.005 deg cells or FRP excess in the 72 h after the event; verdicts reviewed, auto-verdict retained. Placebo: same rule on 2,223 pre-war site-windows.

title: Does orbit see a strike before the news does?
one_liner: No usable lead: the first overpass is a median 2.2 h before the first English GDELT article naming the site, but once ~3 h product latency is added it is 0.8 h after, and the GDELT time is itself an upper bound on when news broke.

GDELT 2.0 raw 15-minute export files

mechanism: VIIRS gives ~2 looks per day per location (three satellites within ~50 min of each other) plus ~3 h NRT latency; news and social media are minutes.
method: For the 11 hits with a GDELT timestamp: first detection overpass time minus first 15-minute GDELT export URL naming the site. Abqaiq 2019 as a historical check.

results.metric: median (IQR) overpass minus first news, hours
median with 3 h NRT latency added
only event with a reported strike clock time (Lavan): detection minus strike
Abqaiq 14 Sep 2019: first overpass after attack

controls: Latency reported both as overpass time and as data-availability time.
caveats: GDELT English URL slugs miss wires, liveblogs, Farsi/Arabic and social media, so true news times are earlier; one -19.5 h value is a date ambiguity; the 3 h latency is assumed, not measured.

title: Can Sentinel-2 SWIR or Sentinel-1 backscatter recover the strikes VIIRS missed at flaring sites?
one_liner: No. Both positive controls are recovered (Tehran Rey burn scar is the top blob site-wide; Fujairah tank damage is the top Sentinel-1 blob at +26 h with zero placebo blobs that size), but Ras Laffan and South Pars remain misses or ambiguous: the damage is sub-pixel at 20 m, the first clear optical scene came 11-31 days later, and novel heat cannot be separated from emergency flaring.

mechanism: 20 m SWIR resolves heat inside process units and burn scars; C-band backscatter changes when metal structures collapse.

Blind whole-site blob ranking, then distance to reported location.

title: Do flare changes lead oil prices, spreads or tanker equities?
one_liner: No. Round 1: Brent leads the flare index by a day, permutation p=0.20, differenced r=-0.23; the markets agent then ran 46 pre-registered tests with a 10,000-draw max-stat permutation and FDR and none survived.

Markets agent: pre-registered max-stat permutation with FDR across 46 market tests (reported to us, not rerun here).

title: Do the validations lean on satellite outage weeks?
one_liner: No. Suomi-NPP was dark 27 Jul-10 Aug 2022 and for five shorter windows in 2024-2026; the country pipeline already excluded those days, the US pipeline did not and was fixed, and every headline statistic moves by less than 0.07 when outage months are removed.

mechanism: An outage scored as zero detections fakes a simultaneous collapse across all regions.
method: Per-satellite daily detection counts summed over 16 countries (2012-2024) and over the Gulf pull (2025-26, all three satellites); day flagged if zero or under 25% of a 31-day rolling median; flagged days +-1 removed; months under 15 valid days dropped; headline stats recomputed with every outage-touching month removed.
